text.p: Metrocall Inc and ProNet Inc said on Monday that they signed a definitive merger agreement under which ProNet would merge into Metrocall.
The new company is expected to create the second largest paging company in the U.S., with over 4 million subscribers, the companies said.
Neither company could be immediately reached to comment further.

Under terms of the deal, which the companies said they expect to complete by late 1997, Metrocall will issue about 12.3 million shares of its common stock -- or 0.9 shares for each share of ProNet common stock.

Dallas-based ProNet has about 12.6 million shares outstanding, and agreements to issue approximately 1.1 million additional shares. It will appoint three directors to Metrocall's board, including its chairman and CEO, Jackie Kimzey, Metrocall said.
Metrocall will have 11 directors on its board.

ProNet operates out of five regional hubs: New York, Chicago, Charlotte, Houston and Northern California. The company has about 1.4 million paging units in service, and has over 50 retail stores marketed under the name "ProNet Communications to Go."
The deal is subject to the approval of ProNet's and Metrocall's stockholders. Metrocall stockholders must also approve an increase in Metrocall's common shares to 80 million.

The deal is also subject to other terms and conditions, including regulatory approvals, consents by Metrocall's banks, and approval of certain pending securities litigation settlements involving ProNet.
If the deal falls through, ProNet will pay a termination fee of $4 million.
Metrocall also has an option to acquire up to 2,450,000 shares of ProNet common stock, representing about 19.4 percent of current shares, at a price of $5.40 per share.
The option is exercisable in the event ProNet's board withdraws its approval of the merger or accepts a competing offer.

Stockholders representing approximately 32 percent of Metrocall's common stock have agreed to vote their shares in favour of the merger and an increase in authorised Metrocall common shares, Metrocall said.

Metrocall also said it will refinance ProNet's existing bank debt through borrowings under its $350 million credit facility. It will also assume ProNet's $100 million, 11 7/8% Senior Subordinated Notes due 2005.
The deal is terminable by either party if it does not close by March 31.
The deal is also terminable by Metrocall if ProNet's annualised operating cash flow as of any two months prior to closing is less than 80 percent of target cash flow, Metrocall said.
